title: Verify remote binaries by source-file SHA256, not mtime; an annotated tag is not a commit
symptom: 'The binary was built at 20:05:01, before the fix commit at 20:05:47' is contested; version checks report the wrong revision.
root_cause: Remote app directories are often not git repositories (no .git), so neither git nor timestamps prove what is compiled; upstream release tags (v0.7.0) are tag objects pointing at the real commit.
minimal_fix: For each file changed by the fix, compare SHA256 of the remote source against the local commit versions, and confirm the build log compiled them; record profiles as tag + resolved commit (e.g. v0.7.0 -> dd169f.., master_ghj 7e40c5bb).
validation: Hash equality plus build-log evidence settled the stale-binary dispute.
avoid: Resolving version disputes by rebuilding blindly or by trusting file mtimes.

parameters.check: SHA256 of changed files vs commit; record tag + resolved commit
